chapter: Russell's band, records and Armstrong in the studio
title: Many good New York trumpeters
summary: Holmes says there was no shortage of trumpeters and none outstanding, naming Bobby Stark and Rex Stewart.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Now he at that time was probably the trumpeter in New York.
No, they had a lot of trumpeters in New York. But he wasn't the trumpeter.
I mean, he was one of the top.

He was a good trumpeter. He was one of the good ones. And there was a lot of them, a lot of good ones. There was never no shortage of trying to find a good trumpeter. There was Bobby Stark, we had what's his name, who used to be with Fletcher, the fat....
No. A short, fat one. He was with Fletcher, he was with Chick, he was with Russell's band -- he was with the band playing "Old Man River."
Rex Stewart. There was a lot of trumpet players. But they was all in the same classification. One was no more outstanding than the other.
